lessons.title: Workplace exposure in grinding, batching and mixing
lessons.html:
Workplace exposure in grinding, batching and mixing

In this workplace module you apply mixed feed production skills on the job over a sustained period. You work with a mentor in the production area and build evidence that you can produce feed to specification, safely and consistently.

Processes to be exposed to

  • Reading and interpreting production schedules and batch tickets.
  • Confirming formulation versions and bin allocations.
  • Operating and checking hammer mills or roller mills, including screen checks and changes.
  • Automatic batching of majors and minors.
  • Hand-adding micro-ingredients, premixes and, where your mill makes them, medicaments.
  • Liquid addition.
  • Mixer operation, discharge and surge bin management.
  • Sampling mixed feed and mixer uniformity testing.
  • Changeovers, sequencing and flushing.
  • Cleaning schedules for mixers, screws and bins.

A typical shift for a production learner

  1. Attend the briefing and note the products for the shift.
  2. Do pre-start checks with your mentor and record them.
  3. Run batches, comparing target and actual weights.
  4. Perform hand-adds and sign the records.
  5. Take scheduled samples and label them.
  6. Handle at least one changeover with flushing, under supervision.
  7. Clean down and complete handover notes.

Evidence to collect

  • Copies or references of batch reports and hand-add records you completed.
  • Mentor observation checklists for each process.
  • A record of a changeover with flush, signed by your mentor.
  • A short report on a deviation you were involved in, with actions taken.

Ask your mentor to explain the formulation for at least one product: why each ingredient is there and which micro-ingredients are critical. This makes the batching steps meaningful and helps you spot mistakes.

lessons.title: Demonstrating competent and safe practice
lessons.html:
Demonstrating competent and safe practice

What competence looks like

AreaYou can show that you
PreparationConfirm product, formula version, bins, premixes and equipment condition before starting
GrindingRun the mill within load range, check grind and act on sudden changes
BatchingSpot out-of-tolerance weights and follow the deviation procedure
Hand-addAdd the right micro-ingredient, correctly weighed, at the right step, every time
MixingApply full dry and wet mix times and correct liquid addition
ChangeoverFollow the sequence and flushing rules, clean where needed, record
RecordsComplete accurate, legible records during the shift, not afterwards

Safety behaviours

  • Lock out before opening mixer, mill or screw covers.
  • Use lifting aids for premix bags; wear dust masks and gloves for micro-ingredients.
  • Keep the hand-add area clean and organised so the wrong bag cannot be picked up.
  • Report any guard missing, interlock fault or hazard immediately.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Starting before confirming the formulation version.
  • Adding a premix from the wrong product because bags were left from the last run.
  • Shortening mix time to catch up.
  • Forgetting to record a flush batch.
  • Filling records at the end of the shift from memory.

Reflection

Write short notes on what went well, what was difficult and how you solved it. Discuss these with your mentor. Reflection shows that you understand why the process works, not only how to press buttons.

Key points

  • This module builds evidence of consistent, on-the-job competence.
  • Confirm formula, bins and premixes before every run.
  • Never shorten mix times or compensate weights.
  • Keep the hand-add area organised to prevent wrong additions.
  • Complete records during the shift and reflect with your mentor.
